AH-001.title: The Kneeling Archer King
AH-001.historical_description: This coin is a symbolic recreation of one of the most iconic motifs found on ancient Achaemenid coinage: a king captured kneeling mid-stride, bow drawn. The image symbolized the eternal readiness, power, and majesty of the Persian empire.
AH-001.story: Frozen in gold is a moment from Iran's endless epic: a king neither standing still nor at war, but forever poised at the threshold of both. A movement locked in metal, a reminder that in ancient Persia, power lived in the silence of a drawn bow.

AH-002.title: The Lion and the Bull
AH-002.historical_description: Faithfully inspired by the famous Persepolis relief, this coin depicts the lion locked in combat with the bull — one of the most enduring images of ancient Persian art, long interpreted as a symbol of the New Year (Nowruz) and the renewal of life and power.
AH-002.story: Two forces of nature, forever bound in struggle: the lion's fury against the bull's raw strength. Carved in gold, this eternal contest speaks of the cycles that ancient Persia believed governed the world — destruction giving way, always, to renewal.

AH-003.title: The Winged Bull
AH-003.historical_description: The winged bull was a guardian figure found across ancient Near Eastern civilizations, from Assyria to Persia — a hybrid being believed to stand watch over gates, palaces, and thresholds between the mortal and divine worlds.
AH-003.story: Half earth, half sky — the winged bull walks the line between worlds. A silent sentinel cast in gold, watching over what came before and what is yet to come.
